title: What scrolling in bed does to your brain, hour by hour (Vex explainer in her dorm, Derek cameo; Scribe: Finish now; Sua voice)

voice.name: Sua shy voice (generic Fish library voice)

beats.say: Scrolling in bed at night. Here's what it actually does to your brain, hour by hour.
Midnight. Blue light from your screen holds back melatonin, your sleep hormone, about twice as long as green light.
One AM. A study of forty-five thousand students found every extra hour on a screen in bed cost about twenty-four minutes of sleep.
And fifty-nine percent higher odds of insomnia.
Derek downstairs is learning that the hard way. Cute.
Two AM, and my bio homework's still due at nine.
So I open Scribe. It writes the page in my handwriting, graph and all, and I tap finish now.
Two-ten. That's eighteen hours awake, which can test about as badly as being tipsy.
Pull an all-nighter, and your brain's ability to make new memories can drop by up to forty percent.
So put the phone down. Go to sleep. I'll know.
